title: Measurement: Volume and Surface Area of Prisms, Cylinders, Cones and Spheres
seo_title: Grade 10 Measurement Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Revise the volume and surface areas of right-prisms and cylinders; study the effect on volume and surface area when multiplying any dimension by a constant factor k; calculate the volume and surface areas of spheres, right pyramids and right cones.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 10 measurement worksheets: volume and surface area of cylinders, cones and spheres, and multiplying dimensions by k. 100 questions with memos.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Cylinder: V = πr²h. Cone: V = ⅓πr²h. Sphere: V = 43πr³.
  • Use the radius, not the diameter.
  • If every length is multiplied by k, area is multiplied by k² and volume by k³.
  • Give units: cm² for area, cm³ for volume.

Examples

Example

Cone, r = 3 cm, h = 10 cm

⅓ × π × 9 × 10

Answer: 94,2 cm³

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
DiameterHalve it to get the radius.
The ⅓A cone is ⅓ of a cylinder.
k or k³Volume scales by k³.

items.q: Two similar parallelograms have corresponding sides of 4 cm and 7 cm. The smaller one has an area of 96 cm². Find the area of the larger one.
items.e: Area scale factor = (7 ÷ 4)2 = 4916. 96 × 4916 = 294 cm².

items.e: Area ratio = (length ratio)2 = 22 : 32 = 4 : 9.

items.q: Two similar cylinders have heights 2 cm and 10 cm. The smaller one has a surface area of 8 cm². Find the surface area of the larger one.
items.e: Surface area is an area, so square the scale factor: (10 ÷ 2)2 = 25. 8 × 25 = 200 cm².

items.q: A silo is a cylinder with radius 5 m and height 10 m, topped by a hemisphere. Find its volume in terms of π.
items.e: Cylinder: π × 5² × 10 = 250π. Hemisphere: ⅔π × 5³ = 2503π. Total: 1 0003π m³.

items.q: Two stacks of 11 coins have the same height. One stack is straight and the other leans to one side. Each coin has radius 11 mm and the stacks are 22 mm tall. How do their volumes compare?
c: The straight stack has more volume
The leaning stack has more volume
items.e: Cavalieri's principle: same height and the same cross-section at every level means the same volume. π × 11² × 22 = 2 662π. They are equal (2 662π mm³ each).

items.q: The radius and the height of a cone are both multiplied by 2. By what factor does the volume change?
items.e: Volume is three dimensions, so it changes by the cube of the scale factor: 2³ = 8.

items.q: A cylindrical tin has radius 5 cm and height 12 cm. What is its capacity to the nearest millilitre? (1 cm³ = 1 mℓ)
A cylindrical water tank has radius 50 cm and height 1,2 m. How many litres does it hold, to the nearest litre?
items.e: Work in cm: π × 50² × 120 = 942 477,8 cm³. 1 000 cm³ = 1 litre, so 942 litres.

items.q: A cylinder has volume 500 cm³ and radius 5 cm. What is its height, to 1 decimal place?
A sphere has volume 36π cm³. What is its radius?
items.e: ⁴⁄₃πr³ = 36π, so r³ = 27 and r = 3 cm.

items.q: A cone and a cylinder have the same radius and height. How many cones of water fill the cylinder?
items.e: A cone is ⅓ of the cylinder with the same base and height, so 3 cones fill it.

items.q: An ice cream cone has radius 3 cm and height 10 cm, with a hemisphere of ice cream on top of radius 3 cm. Find the total volume in terms of π.
items.e: Cone: ⅓ × π × 9 × 10 = 30π. Hemisphere: ⅔ × π × 27 = 18π. Total: 48π cm³.

items.q: A ball has diameter 22 cm. What is its volume to the nearest cm³?
If the radius of a sphere doubles, what happens to its volume?
items.e: Volume depends on r³, and 2³ = 8, so it is multiplied by 8.

items.q: If the height of a cylinder doubles and the radius stays the same, what happens to its volume?
items.e: V = πr²h and only h doubles, so it doubles.

items.q: If the radius of a cylinder doubles and the height stays the same, what happens to its volume?
items.e: V depends on r², and 2² = 4, so it is multiplied by 4.
